messages:
alex.k: :rotating_light: getting paged — huge spike hitting /v1/sessions/login and /v1/batch/generate from a small set of IP ranges. Traffic looks automated, ~120 req/s sustained, 20k requests in 5m. Errors are mostly 429 and some 502 backpressure. Full traces in logs.

jess.sre: oncall here. Paging PD, cutting into triage. Can someone drop the IP list and request patterns?

alex.k: sample user agents: "python-requests/2.28", "curl/7.68.0" and some custom UA headers. IP blocks: 34.88.0.0/16, 52.40.128.0/17, 143.244.0.0/16. Endpoints: POST /v1/sessions/login large bursts, POST /v1/batch/generate with long ctx.

incident-bot: Incident created: I-2026-1800102468 — "mass login/scraper traffic detected". Severity: P2. Notifying security and infra.

priya.sec: thanks. I'm seeing credential-stuffing patterns on login attempts: many different emails, same IPs. We should enable WAF rule set and add rate limit for /v1/sessions/login immediately. Recommend temporary global quota per IP and per-account lockout after 5 failed attempts/min.

tom.infra: I can push quick WAF blocks and proxy-level rate limits. Plan: 1) Add WAF block for listed IP CIDRs 2) Apply req/s limit: 5r/s per IP for /v1/sessions/login 3) Apply dynamic token bucket for /v1/batch/generate to drop heavy batch requests 4) If still noisy, disable unauth batch endpoints for anonymous keys.

jess.sre: Agreed. Execute in that order. Also enable 503 fallback to keep latency SLO for genuine traffic. Notify product about potential customer hit.

alex.k: executing steps now. Pushing WAF deny for 34.88.0.0/16 and 52.40.128.0/17. CLI: 

```
redwood-waf block --cidr 34.88.0.0/16 --reason "credential-spray"
redwood-waf block --cidr 52.40.128.0/17 --reason "credential-spray"
```

apply rate limit on proxy:
```
proxyctl rate-limit set --route "POST /v1/sessions/login" --limit 5 --burst 10 --scope ip
proxyctl rate-limit set --route "/v1/batch/generate" --limit 10 --burst 20 --scope key
```

incident-bot: WAF rules applied and rate-limit rules accepted.

maya-cs: seeing customer tickets for intermittent 429s. Can you share mitigation plan & ETA?

jess.sre: Replying to CS: temporary rate limits are in place to stop automated abuse. We're blocking identified bot CIDRs and throttling login and batch endpoints. Expected stabilization in 5-10 minutes. We will rollback if we see >5% legitimate failed requests.

priya.sec: also enabling account-level lockouts: cron job to mark account as locked for 15m after 6 failed attempts in 10m window. Pushing rule now.

alex.k: lockout rule applied. Command: 

```
accountsctl policy add --name "temp-lockout" --failed-attempts 6 --window 10m --lock-duration 15m
```

tom.infra: adding token-bucket shaping to /v1/batch/generate cluster-wide to reduce cost impact from long sequences. Setting per-key soft limit 3 concurrent streams, queue depth 8.

deploy-bot: config-update deployed to edge proxies (edge-v2) — 3 nodes rolled, 4 remaining.

jess.sre: monitoring metrics: significant drop in request rate from those CIDRs, overall service errors dropping from 18% -> 2%. Latency stable. Keep watch for false positives.

maya-cs: relayed to several enterprise customers — they acknowledged. One customer (acme-inc) reported failures with our batch endpoint earlier; we've whitelisted their IPs and raised per-key limit for them.

alex.k: added whitelist for acme-inc IPs: 18.205.93.0/24.

priya.sec: quick note — captured payloads indicate credential stuffing; saving indicators to abuseintel. Will open takedown requests with providers for persistent CIDRs.

jess.sre: On-call handoff at 12:00 UTC to alex — current status: mitigations active, traffic normalized but we still see low-level scanning from new ranges. If we continue to see scanning, next steps: escalate to full blocklist and temporarily disable anonymous batch endpoints (public keys).

alex.k: acknowledged. I'll take lead and continue monitoring. Will escalate to P1 if impact to customers >10% or if mitigation fails.

incident-bot: Incident I-2026-1800102468 status changed to: Mitigated. Notes: WAF blocks, proxy rate-limits, account lockouts, whitelist for verified customers.

jess.sre: creating follow-up postmortem stub. Tags: abuse, waf, rate-limits, oncall-handoff. Assigning to priya and alex for investigation and IOC cleanup.

priya.sec: copying logs to secure bucket and starting IOC enrichment. Will include rules for future WAF tuning.

alex.k: leaving final note — cost impact: CPU/GPUs increased by ~12% during spike due to long batch jobs; estimated incremental cost $1.2k for the 2-hour period. We'll propose automated tighter defaults for anonymous batch limits in the postmortem.

maya-cs: customers updated. Closing tickets once postmortem published. :white_check_mark:

jess.sre: thanks team. Marking thread resolved in 2h if no regression.
